title: GPU driver rollback orchestrator and fast reconciliation
author: Aisha Patel
body:
Summary:

This document describes the GPU Driver Rollback Orchestrator (GDRO): an integrated CI/CD + IaC pattern and operator that performs safe, fast, and auditable rollbacks of GPU driver & kernel-level components across Redwood inference fleets. It focuses on minimizing production impact for inference traffic, providing deterministic reconciliation after failed driver updates, and integrating with our Terraform modules, image signing pipeline, and bake/canary gates.

Goals:
- Reduce mean time to recovery (MTTR) for driver-level regressions to under 15 minutes for affected regions.
- Avoid broad node drains when only a software rollback is needed.
- Provide an auditable, RBAC-gated path for rollbacks that integrates with billing and tenant-impact reporting.
- Automate reconciliation to detect partial rollbacks and self-heal to a consistent fleet state.

Scope and non-goals:
- Scope: GPU node driver packages (NVIDIA/CUDA drivers, kernel modules, accelerator firmware where supported), node-level boot-time configs, and the associated machine images/signatures. Targets: hosted inference GPU pools and Dedicated fleet pools managed by Redwood.
- Non-goals: hardware-level repairs, firmware requiring physical intervention, or tenant application-level rollbacks.

Background and motivation:
Driver updates are one of the highest-risk changes for latency and stability regressions. Historically we've responded with broad rolling reverts or full cluster drains which are slow and expensive. GDRO provides a pattern that: (1) orchestrates targeted rollbacks per node or node-pool, (2) verifies post-rollback health using PV/Warm pool and inference synthetic checks, and (3) reconciles state differences between Terraform, the image registry, and the running fleet.

Architecture overview (text diagram):
- CI/CD pipeline (Buildkite) -> signed driver artifact + AMI/Container image -> Terraform image promotion -> Fleet controller (GDRO Operator) -> Node agent (gdro-agent) -> Observability/Telemetry (Prometheus, Honeycomb)

Key components and responsibilities:
1) Build & Sign pipeline (CI):
   - Produces driver artifact + image with SBOM, signature, and metadata (driver-version, kernel-compat).
   - Publishes to internal registry with a promotion tag stage: canary -> promoted
   - If CVE or hotfix, CI issues a Release with change-log and owner contact.

2) Terraform and IaC integration:
   - Image/driver versions are captured in terraform variables (gpu_image_version, driver_hash) and stored in the git-backed tf workspace per-region.
   - GDRO exposes a small Terraform provider data source we maintain (tfdata.gdro_target) that can be used by promotion plays to pin rollback candidates.
   - Promotion flow: promote_image -> terraform plan -> apply (can be auto-approved for canaries, manual for global).

3) GDRO Operator (control plane):
   - Runs as a central service in control-plane account with cross-account read/write to fleet accounts via short-lived roles.
   - Receives rollback request (API/CLI or automated from pipeline) and creates a RollbackPlan CR (conceptually).
   - Selects targets using selectors (pool, label, region, taints) and computes minimal-change plan.

4) gdro-agent (node-side):
   - Light-weight daemon that can: fetch signed driver artifacts, apply driver rollback (with pre-checks), run dry-run kernel module unload/load, and report status + logs to control plane.
   - Supports safe kernel switch strategies where supported (kexec/safe-module-unload) and fallback to cordon+restart if required.

5) Observability & verification:
   - Post-rollback verification suite includes: node-level GPU health, kv-cache warmup time, 95th/99th inference latency synthetic probe, and tenant error-rate delta.
   - Metrics emitted: gdro.rollback.duration_seconds, gdro.rollback.success_count, gdro.rollback.verified_count, gdro.reconcile.inconsistent_nodes.

Safety and gating strategy:
- Preflight checks: ensure node telemetry is healthy, no ongoing critical tenant migrations, and warm-pool capacity >= 15% for region.
- Canary rollout default: 3 nodes across AZs with 10-minute verification window.
- Progressive rollout: 3 -> 10 -> 25 -> 100% (configurable per-policy).
- Automatic halt and rollback policy: if latency or error-rate exceeds configured thresholds (by default: latency 95th increase > 12%, error-rate increase > 2% absolute or > 50% relative) the plan will be immediately reversed.
- Forced manual abort requires 2 approvers from SRE and Infra owners.

Terraform & CI/CD Runbook (step-by-step):
1) Release produces a promoted image with rollback candidate tag, and the pipeline posts a Rollback Intent ticket in the release board if required.
2) Trigger: via REST API or CLI: gdro rollback start --target-pool gpu-inference-eu-west-1 --from-version 2026.01.10 --to-version 2026.01.04 --reason "latency regression"
3) GDRO performs preflight and calculates target node list; it writes a RollbackPlan artifact to the tf workspace and posts a Change event (audit).
4) Canary stage: agent downloads driver, performs dry-run unload/compat-check, applies driver, runs verification probes (5m probe + 2m settle). If green, proceed to next stage.
5) Progressive stage: after each cohort completes verification, terraform image variable is updated in the regional workspace by GDRO and applied by the rollout pipeline to capture desired-state drift.
6) Failure path: GDRO triggers apply of the previous known-good image, marks nodes with failure tags, and opens incident with pre-filled checklist for oncall.

Operator reconciliation behavior and eventual consistency rules:
- Periodic reconciliation loop (default 2m): operator compares desired_image in terraform state, promoted image tag in registry, and node reported version.
- If mismatch and node shows last-update-failure, operator will attempt one soft-retry (agent fetch and reapply). If still mismatched and node in critical tenant path, escalate to runbook.
- Reconciliation must be idempotent: every plan includes a plan-id and signature to prevent double-applying.

Runbook: Immediate actions for oncall (short):
1) If alert gdro.rollback.failed or gdro.reconcile.inconsistent_nodes > 0: run gdro status --plan <id>
2) Check canary telemetry dashboard: latency, error-rates, kv-cache hit-rate, node GPU temp.
3) If still in canary stage and failing: gdro rollback abort --plan <id> (automated reverse).
4) If nodes failing reconciliation after abort: cordon affected nodes: kubectl cordon <node>, and run node-reimage playbook (link in related_pages).
5) Escalation matrix: SRE oncall -> Infra lead -> Product owner (if tenant impact > 5%).

Security & compliance notes:
- All rollback actions are audited in our central audit log with actor, reasons, and signatures.
- Only members with gdro.rollback role (RBAC) can run global rollbacks; canary-level rollbacks require 'gdro.canary' permissions.
- Signed artifacts are mandatory; unsigned rollbacks are rejected.

Operational metrics & SLOs to monitor:
- MTTR for driver rollback (target < 15m).
- Percentage of rollbacks that fully reconcile without manual intervention (target > 90%).
- False-positive halts (rollout stopped but no regression found) < 5% of rollouts.

Owner and maintenance:
- Primary owner: infra/ci-cd team (Aisha Patel).
- SRE owns verification probes and dashboard (Marco Silva).
- Security review cadence: quarterly for signing keys and tf-provider scope.

Implementation checklist (short):
- [x] gdro-agent prototype deployed to canary nodes
- [x] CI image & signature metadata added to Buildkite pipeline
- [x] Terraform data-source and provider shim implemented (internal repo: infra/tf-provider-gdro)
- [x] Metrics and dashboards onboarded
- [ ] Auto-approval policy review with legal for tenant-impact reporting

Appendix: Example CLI commands:
- Start a rollback:
  gdro rollback start --pool gpu-inference-us-east-1 --from 2026.02.08 --to 2026.01.22 --reason "perf regression"
- Inspect plan:
  gdro plan show --id plan-20260208-001
- Abort ongoing rollback:
  gdro rollback abort --id plan-20260208-001 --force

Related artifacts and links:
- Terraform provider: git@repo:redwood/infra/tf-provider-gdro (module README contains example data source usage)
- Buildkite pipeline: bk/gdro-driver-publish (recipe: build -> sign -> promote)
- Dashboards: Grafana/gdro-rollout-overview, SLO/gdro-reconcile-success
